issue.title: Grok monitor follow-up stayed RUNNING for ten hours after backgrounding final context
issue.description: Proposed by the Landing section of plan:202610/green_gates_ship_0_18_0.md; corroborating phase sase-1lh.7.5.4.3.3.1 note #1. Existing active sase-11t is Codex gate-turn integrity and not a proven cause. No general release-watcher repair is needed for this report: follow-up-free monitor pattern now releases the lander. Root cause unknown, size large.

task_type_fields.impact: A closed phase bead does not release its epic lander while its agent session stays RUNNING. Investigate bounded tool completion/idle supervision without killing legitimate monitored work; regress the failure once root-caused.
task_type_fields.location: Grok provider follow-up sase-1lh.7.5.4.3.2--2; sase final context and provider tool completion
task_type_fields.repro: Historical incident, not newly recreated: plan:202610/green_gates_ship_0_18_0.md records stale plan_digest rejection, then sase final context backgrounded after 30s, no tool calls after 2026-10-17T07:58Z, still RUNNING about ten hours later. Phase sase-1lh.7.5.4.3.3.1 note #1 confirms it killed the stuck follow-up and its parked lander. sase chat show --basename gh_sase_org__sase-ace_run-sase_1lh_7_5_4_3_2__2-261017_034534 recovers the local prompt but has an empty Response; use retained provider/tool logs to establish the stall mechanism.

issue.creation_reason: The approved green_gates_ship_0_18_0 landing explicitly requires tracking the previous watch follow-up hang. Search across all statuses and recent tasks found no owner; the SIGTERM hardening fixes kill behavior, not the stalled provider.
